title: We see broader adoption of Bitcoin: Bill
description:
Sean Bill, co-founder and chief investment officer at Bitcoin Standard Treasury Company, joins BNN Bloomberg to discuss crypto amid geopolitical uncertainty.

asr.full_text: Despite being a bit flat today, crypto has seen a significant jump over the past few weeks. That move comes as tensions in the Middle East rise and oil prices climb. Bitcoin has continued to draw interest amid the ongoing geopolitical uncertainty. Joining us now to break this all down is Sean Bill, co-founder and CIO of BSTR. Sean, thanks very much for joining us. Thanks for having me, Roger. I appreciate being here. MIKE GREEN I mean, Bitcoin and crypto has always a roller coaster. We've known even more. So one this year, hasn't it? SEAN HANSEN Oh, absolutely. Yeah. I mean, this is actually a relatively mild drawdown for Bitcoin this year, down about 38-40% from the peak. For those of us who have been in Bitcoin for a long time, this is relatively tame. We've seen some other declines into the 60s and 80s, and even in the early days. So, I think as this sector has grown and as the market cap of Bitcoin has expanded, we've actually seen the volatility come down quite a bit. And are you surprised, considering with what's unfolding in the Middle East, that it hasn't been as volatile? I think that a lot of folks view Bitcoin as almost like a digital gold. It makes sense to me that it's finding a bottom here with all the activity going on in the Suez Canal and the price action we've seen on Gold, although it's been a little more volatile lately. Bitcoin's very similar. It basically functions a lot like gold. It's limited supply. It's convertible into any currency in the world, and those two functions make it like a digital gold that you can move in your wallet and that you carry on your phone. Any concerns about broader macro issues with crypto right now? I think the one main issue would be what's going to happen within the two-money supply. What we're seeing here in the Middle East and with potentially higher or energy prices and what have you, could actually lead to higher rates. That would be probably negative for Bitcoin. However, on the flip side of that, you know, the U.S. government's going to have to replenish all those armaments that they've been spending in the Middle East. And that could lead to additional money supply growth. So, if we see money supply growth, that usually is very positive for Bitcoin. And with that Senate crypto bill that's working its way somewhere and so i guess it's at the center yeah it's at the senate banking committee right now it's uh on its on its way uh how important is that and is it shaping up to be something that will be good uh for cryptocurrency well we think it's really important actually um you know the genius act went through and that kind of laid the groundwork for stable coins. And this is important, because under the prior administration there was kind of a negative tilt towards digital assets. And so, we lost a lot of that industry to Singapore and Switzerland and other countries. And so, what we've seen with the actions from Congress and the Senate is they're really trying to create an operating framework for folks to be able to operate legally here in the US. And we think that's a really strong positive. I mean, we want to see the US as the financial capital of the world. You know, to do that, you have to update the regulation to fit today's modern age of digital assets. Crypto always seems like there's a bit of an outlaw feel to it and will people come into the fold if that goes through? Yeah. I think back in 2019, I originally proposed adding Bitcoin to our pension funds here in California when I was the chief investment officer at Santa Clara. Back then people looked at you like you had three heads, like you're crazy. This asset actually has a very low correlation to other assets. As a strong fat right tail in terms of the return distribution. It actually makes a lot of sense for endowments foundation's, pension funds to have a smidge of Bitcoin in their portfolio. We've seen broader adoption now. It used to just be the Virginia Fairfax folks, Houston firefighters, and Santa Clara that really had any exposure, but now you're seeing it be a relatively hot topic within the pension community, and within the endowments and foundations who are probably one or two steps ahead of the pensions. most of those do have some exposure to bitcoin i'm just seeing the story about uh satsuma the uh bitcoin accumulator and shareholders now pushing for it to sell all the tokens and wind down is that a concern or is that a one-off do you feel i think that's potentially a one-off but i mean if you're you know i think that this is a game where you're going to have just just like, I guess, we stepped back and we think about technology, zero net marginal cost for each additional unit that you're investing and trading and generally, these models tend to consolidate with large players. That's our view. We think that there will be a couple of large winners in the Bitcoin space. Bitcoin Standard Treasury, our company we think will be one of those winners. It will be the second largest Bitcoin Treasury likely when it comes to public in June. Just like you have one or two winners in retail with Amazon or Shopify, or one or two winners in social with maybe META and X, or Search with Google. We think that will be the same thing in the Bitcoin treasury space. What's the difference between yours? And what gives you the confidence compared to Setsuma? What's the difference? Oh, I think we're very different. I mean, you know, first off, we have, you know, Adam Back and myself as co-founders started the Bitcoin Standard Treasury Company. We raised, you know, about $5.1 billion at the time in two days. We have a very experienced corporate company and we have done a really successful network with Bitcoin through AdiCoin. It was our company. We raised about $5.1 billion at the time in two days. We are also our own largest investor. We put 25,000 Bitcoins into seeding the company. I think what we bring to the table is an extraordinarily deep domain expertise within the technology uh bitcoin via atomvac and then this extraordinarily deep domain expertise within the active management of the bitcoin treasury so what we're really trying to do with our treasury is to actively manage that bitcoin and use it as an asset so much like how berkshire hathaway uses stocks and bonds as their asset to grow their business and uh we would like to do that with bitcoin okay we got to wrap it up there, Shamba. Thank you very much for joining us. Thank you for having me. Apeachate it. Shaun Bell, co-founder and C-I-O of BSTR.
